A three-part exhibition at the British Museum, which opens on 21 May and draws together a rich and diverse range of artworks, artifacts, textiles, paintings and photographs from different parts of India and its diaspora.
One section will feature paintings from the courts of Mughal emperors and Rajput princes, including the famous "War of Dhar" series by Nainsukh and the "Princess and the Dragon" from Rajasthani folklore.
Another will showcase miniature court paintings as well as the less well-known havelis — the ornately decorated homes of the mercantile elite — from Rajasthan.
The third part of the exhibition looks at the arriving of the British East India Company, and how Western influences shaped Indian art from the mid-18th to the mid-19th century, highlighting Indian drawings of British industry, trade, politics, and technology.
